answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The karst multiplier is published, charged in vault, and gale lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3012 identities would post 4804 proofs and burn roughly 69 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
